exhibits.title: Spot Price
exhibits.statement: Solana (SOL) traded at $85.6400 as of 2026-11-09 07:42:54 UTC, -0.68% over one hour and -3.88% over twenty-four hours.

exhibits.title: 24-Hour Trading Range
exhibits.statement: Over twenty-four hours the price ranged from $85.5400 to $89.8000; spot sits at 2% of that range.

exhibits.title: Seven-Day Trend
exhibits.statement: Price is -9.22% over seven days. The 24-hour average ($88.2768) is below the 72-hour average ($89.3072). Spot is 11.51% below the seven-day high of $96.7814 and 0.12% above the seven-day low of $85.5400.

exhibits.title: Volatility & Momentum
exhibits.statement: Realized volatility computed from hourly closes is 3.25% per day. The 14-hour relative strength index reads 31.6, conventionally neutral.

exhibits.title: Liquidity
exhibits.statement: Twenty-four-hour trading volume was $2.4 billion, equal to 4.75% of the $50.63 billion market capitalization.

exhibits.title: Market Sentiment
exhibits.statement: The Crypto Fear & Greed Index reads 29 ("Fear"), versus 37 7 days earlier.

exhibits.title: Chainlink Price Feed
exhibits.statement: The Chainlink SOL/USD Data Feed on Ethereum mainnet last reported $85.4435, 30 minutes before the spot quote and -0.23% against the spot price in Exhibit A. Practice positions are entered and settled at this mark.

arguments.text:
May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price of SOL has slipped 0.68% in the last hour and 3.88% in 24 hours, positioning it near the lower bound of its 24‑hour range (2% above the floor) and indicating a price level primed for a rebound as traders seek value at the bottom of the range [Ex. A, B].  

2. Despite a modest 3.25% daily realized volatility, the market exhibits ample liquidity—$2.4 billion traded in 24 hours, representing 4.75% of market cap—providing the depth needed for a sustained upward move without slippage concerns [Ex. D, E].  

3. Sentiment has turned increasingly fearful, with the Fear & Greed Index dropping to 29, a level historically preceding short‑term recoveries, and the Chainlink feed confirming a price floor at $85.44, giving the practice position a secure entry point [Ex. F, G].  

The Bull rests.

May it please the Court.  

1. The spot price of SOL is presently $85.64, sitting just 2 % above the low of its 24‑hour range and 11.51 % below the seven‑day high, indicating that sellers have already driven the market toward the lower bound of recent activity and further downside is statistically more probable than a rebound [Ex. A, B, C].  

2. Realized volatility of 3.25 % per day combined with a RSI of 31.6—well within the neutral zone—shows no over‑bought momentum to fuel a short‑term rally, while the modest volume of $2.4 B relative to market cap suggests limited buying pressure to counteract the existing drift [Ex. D, E].  

3. Market sentiment is firmly in fear, with the Fear & Greed Index at 29, a decline from a week earlier, and the Chainlink feed—our settlement benchmark—prices SOL at $85.44, reinforcing that the price floor is already near the seven‑day low [Ex. F, G].  

The Bear rests.

Your Honor, the Bear’s first point rests on a mis‑reading of the 24‑hour range: Exhibit B shows SOL sits at only 2 % of that range, not 2 % above the low, meaning the price is essentially mid‑range and not “near the lower bound” as claimed [Ex. B]. Moreover, the Bear’s second point ignores the neutral RSI of 31.6, which, while modest, sits well above the oversold threshold of 30 and therefore does not preclude a short‑term bounce; the same neutral reading is reinforced by the modest but still healthy 4.75 % volume‑to‑market‑cap ratio, indicating sufficient liquidity to support upside pressure [Ex. D, E]. Nothing further.

Your Honor, the Bull’s “rebound” thesis collapses on two fronts. First, the price sits just 2 % above the 24‑hour floor yet remains 11.51 % below the seven‑day high, showing no upward momentum; the 72‑hour average still exceeds the 24‑hour average, confirming a downtrend ([Ex. C]). Second, the RSI of 31.6 is not “neutral” but deep in oversold territory, signalling continued weakness rather than a bounce ([Ex. D]). Fear is rising (index 29), but fear alone does not generate buying pressure; it reflects deteriorating sentiment that can sustain declines. Thus the Bull’s optimism lacks evidentiary support. Nothing further.

ruling.holding: The Court finds that a short practice position is warranted for SOL/USD over the next 24 hours.

findings.finding: Spot price is down 3.88% in 24 h and sits near the lower bound of its 24‑hour range
Seven‑day trend is –9.22% with the 24‑hour average below the 72‑hour average, confirming downward momentum
Realized volatility is modest (3.25%/day) and RSI 31.6 indicates oversold conditions, limiting upside bounce potential
Fear & Greed Index at 29 (Fear) shows deteriorating sentiment, which historically supports further declines

ruling.opinion: The exhibits collectively depict a weakening market: price has fallen sharply and remains near its daily low [Ex. A]; the seven‑day trend is negative and short‑term averages are lower than longer ones, confirming a downtrend [Ex. C]; volatility is low and RSI sits in oversold territory, reducing the likelihood of a rebound [Ex. D]; and fear sentiment is elevated, which historically precedes further drops [Ex. F]. Chainlink’s feed merely confirms the current level and does not offset these bearish signals. Accordingly, a short position is justified.
ruling.dissent: Bull argues that the price is effectively mid‑range and that neutral RSI permits a bounce, but the weight of downtrend, oversold RSI, and fear sentiment outweighs that view.
